newsitem.title: USA: USDA's Glickman says CRP limit could tighten wheat.
newsitem.headline: USDA's Glickman says CRP limit could tighten wheat.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Thursday that a plan by a House Appropriations subcommittee to limit new entries to the Conservation Reserve Program could tighten U.S. wheat supplies.

"Idling these additional acres, in combination with this year's adverse weather, could have detrimental effects on future U.S. grain supplies, likely leading to reduced exports and increased imports from Canada," Glickman said in a letter to House Agriculture Committee Chairman Bob Smith (R-Id).
On Wednesday, a House Appropriations subcommittee backed capping new entries to the CRP at 14 million acres this year.
Farmers have offered 25.6 million acres for the reserve. Contracts on 21 million acres expire this fall. USDA has indicated it might accept up to 19 million acres.

"The flood conditions in the Northern Plains and the recent freeze in the Southern Plains have reduced the production potential for the 1997 wheat crop," Glickman said in the letter. "Although the size of the upcoming harvest remains uncertain, a reduced crop would prevent the expected recovery in this season's low carryover stocks."
In the past two weeks, cash market wheat prices have risen about 20 percent, reflecting market concerns about supply.
The proposed CRP restrictions also mean that the Agriculture Department will not be able to enroll more new, environmentally sensitive acreage that has been offered, Glickman said.
The legislation would also disrupt the Agriculture Department's ability to meet its May deadline for informing U.S. farmers about CRP enrollment, he said.
